after: - **Deny beats allow.** If multiple rules match at equal specificity, the strictest autonomy wins (`human-only` > `manual` > `supervised-live` > `supervised-retro` > `autonomous`). That is the strictness ordering, and it binds everywhere an ordering is consulted: this tie-break, any comparator an implementation derives from it, and any surface that ranks or sorts levels. `human-only` heads it because it is strictly more scrutiny than `manual`: `manual` says a human decides and an agent then acts, `human-only` says the human acts, so a tie between the two resolves to the level under which no agent executes. (Amended APRV-185, pending sign-off.) The declared `live_rate` is not part of the ordering
